templates.text: Cardiac septation completes, while renal tubules differentiate and hepatic hematopoiesis shifts to the bone marrow.
The GI tract undergoes rotational fixation, and the hepatic architecture organizes into distinct lobules.
Renal glomeruli mature to filter primitive urine, synchronized with the refinement of cardiac valve leaflets.
Hepatocytes begin glycogen storage as the stomach and intestines establish their definitive mucosal layers.
Cardiac conduction pathways mature, concurrent with the development of functional renal collecting ducts.
The liver's role in bile production initiates alongside the final maturation of the intestinal villi.
Renal cortex and medulla differentiate clearly, while the GI tract completes its mesenteric attachments.
Cardiac myofibrils increase in density, and hepatic sinusoids form a mature vascular network.
GI smooth muscle layers organize into coherent patterns, and renal calyces begin to take shape.
Hepatic ductal plates remodel, as the cardiac chambers achieve their final proportional sizes.
The renal system now produces dilute urine, timed with the stomach's development of glandular pits.
Cardiac neural crest cells complete their migration, ensuring proper outflow tract alignment.
Hepatic lobulation proceeds rapidly, and the intestines commence meconium accumulation.
Renal vascular resistance drops, allowing for increased blood flow to the developing nephrons.
The GI tract exhibits coordinated peristaltic waves, supported by mature enteric nervous plexuses.
Cardiac valve cushions fuse definitively, and hepatocytes initiate plasma protein synthesis.
Renal papillary ducts elongate, while the gastric mucosa develops its characteristic rugal folds.
Hepatic architecture finalizes its portal triads, concurrent with intestinal crypt formation.
The cardiac foramen ovale flap forms, and renal tubular function begins to regulate electrolytes.
GI epithelial barrier integrity strengthens, synchronized with the liver's expanding metabolic capacity.
Renal corpuscles achieve mature filtration capacity within {days} days of structural completion.
Cardiac trabeculae compact to form the ventricular walls, as the liver assumes fetal glucose homeostasis.
The hepatic biliary tree canalizes, and the stomach musculature develops its three distinct layers.
Renal ureteric bud branching concludes, establishing the final count of collecting ducts.
GI mucosal goblet cells appear, secreting mucus to protect the newly lined intestinal lumen.
Cardiac coronary arteries complete their intramyocardial course, ensuring robust myocardial perfusion.
Hepatic stellate cells populate the space of Disse, and renal juxtaglomerular apparatuses form.
The intestinal lengthening and coiling process finishes, creating the definitive loops within the abdomen.
Renal calyces and pelvis expand, preparing for the continuous flow of fetal urine production.
Cardiac autonomic innervation matures, regulating a steady fetal heart rate amidst systemic growth.
